solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Dirty power tool to repair coastal structure

parts.note: something dirty is black with grime

indicators.note: repairing a tool means taking it apart and putting it back together, so the letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: Someone is told to fix a filthy power tool so it can be used on a seaside building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to repair' is the anagram signal. Blackpool Tower is a landmark on the seafront of the English resort of Blackpool.
explanation.definitionFit: The tower stands on the Lancashire seafront, a landmark built beside the sea.

clue.text: Characters linger around to keep dry before end of deluge

indicators.note: the shuffled letters hold the next pieces inside them
the word linger is turned around and reshuffled into a new order
the dry piece comes ahead of the next one

parts.note: teetotal, abbreviated TT, means not drinking: dry

indicators.note: only the final letter of deluge is used

explanation.surface: Someone lingers about trying to stay dry before a downpour finishes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' makes LERING from the fodder, and 'to keep' splits it after its second letter. TT, for teetotal, is the usual crossword dry.
explanation.definitionFit: Lettering means written or printed characters, such as those on a sign.

clue.text: Squadron is body that's not totally complete

indicators.note: the word is cut short of its final letter

parts.note: a body is a corpse

explanation.surface: A body of airmen is described as being not quite up to strength.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not totally complete' removes the last letter, E, from CORPSE.
explanation.definitionFit: A corps is a military unit, loosely comparable to a squadron as an organised body of troops.

clue.text: Shown around lake of French region

parts.note: something shown has been proven
ca, for circa, is Latin for around
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: Someone has been shown around a lake in some part of France.
explanation.walkthrough: CA is circa, the Latin 'about' used before dates.
explanation.definitionFit: Provençal describes things belonging to Provence in south-eastern France.

clue.text: Signs small fish is coming to the surface

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising to the surface means the letters read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: Nemo is the clownfish of the animated film Finding Nemo

explanation.surface: A sign of something is spotted as a little fish rises to the top of the water.
explanation.walkthrough: S plus NEMO reads upwards as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Omens are signs or portents of what is to come.

clue.text: Toiled lifting painting, a devil to shift

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifting raises the letters so they read upwards

parts.note: a painting is a piece of art

indicators.note: the letters of a devil are shifted into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone hauls a painting upstairs and finds it fiendishly hard to move.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lifting' turns ART into TRA; 'to shift' rearranges A DEVIL into VAILED.
explanation.definitionFit: To travail is to labour hard, so travailed is a synonym of toiled.

clue.text: 15 in the future will occupy Mars, employing nanobots initially

indicators.note: the opening letter of each of these five words is taken

explanation.surface: A science-fiction forecast that people will settle Mars with the help of nanobots.
explanation.walkthrough: 15 is HEAD GIRLS; girls grow up to be adult females, which is what they will be in the future.
explanation.definitionFit: Girls become adult females as they grow up, so that is what the pupils at 15 will one day be.

clue.text: Foreign troops once forced to capture king within year in Revolution

indicators.note: a revolution turns the whole construction round so it reads backwards
the forced-plus-king piece sits inside the year abbreviation
the word for forced takes the king letter into it

parts.note: made means forced, as in made to do something
R is the abbreviation for king, from Latin rex

explanation.surface: An occupying army was compelled to seize a monarch during a year of uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: The built string YMRADER is turned round by 'in Revolution'; the capital R in Revolution hints at the Russian one.
explanation.definitionFit: The Red Army was the Soviet Union's army, a foreign force from a British viewpoint, and no longer exists.

clue.text: Introduction to philosophy penned by French author for academic world

indicators.note: the opening letter is held inside the writer's name, as if written into it

parts.note: Albert Camus was a French writer and philosopher

indicators.note: only the first letter of philosophy is used

explanation.surface: A French writer pens a primer on philosophy for scholars.
explanation.definitionFit: A campus is a university's grounds, standing for the academic world as a whole.

clue.text: Beam cut at near edge to make post

indicators.note: the letter at the front end of the word is removed

parts.note: a rafter is a sloping roof beam

explanation.surface: A carpenter trims a beam at one end to make an upright post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Post' looks like a wooden upright, matching the beam; it is the Latin-derived prefix meaning later.
explanation.definitionFit: Post is the prefix meaning later in time, as in postwar, which is a synonym of the answer.

clue.text: Welcoming duck coop provided with protection

parts.note: in cricket, a duck is a score of nothing, O
a coop for animals is a pen
armed means equipped with weapons to defend oneself

explanation.surface: A duck's coop is fitted with defences.
explanation.walkthrough: A duck is a batsman's score of zero in cricket, written as O.
explanation.definitionFit: An open-armed greeting is warm and welcoming, like an embrace.

clue.text: Offering journalists front and back of issue

parts.note: journalists collectively are the press

indicators.note: the first and last letters of issue are taken

explanation.surface: Journalists are offered the front and back pages of a magazine issue.
explanation.definitionFit: A pressie is informal British slang for a present, a gift or offering.

clue.text: Checkout assistant, perhaps, primarily serves one packing containers

indicators.note: the first letter of serves is used

parts.note: a canner is a person who packs food into cans

explanation.surface: A shop worker at the till mainly serves, and also packs things into boxes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Checkout assistant' suggests a person, but the device at the till is meant; 'perhaps' flags the joke.
explanation.definitionFit: A barcode reader at the till does the job of a checkout assistant, so it is a whimsical example.

clue.text: Male boring this ground is manual worker

indicators.note: the male letter bores into the other letters, sitting inside them
ground means crushed and reformed, so the letters of this are reordered

explanation.surface: A man finds digging this patch of earth dull, as a labourer would.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' rearranges THIS into SITH, and M goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A smith, such as a blacksmith, works metal with their hands, a classic manual trade.

clue.text: Changing form, Sir glad he gets trustworthy pupils

indicators.note: the letters of these words change their shape into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A schoolmaster is pleased when he gets reliable pupils as the class changes.
explanation.walkthrough: A form is a British school class, which makes 'Changing form' read naturally.
explanation.definitionFit: Head girls are senior pupils chosen to lead a school because they can be relied on.

clue.text: Vessel everyone backed to cut piracy at sea

indicators.note: the reversed piece cuts into the shuffled letters
at sea means confused, so piracy's letters are thrown into disorder
backed means turned back, read from right to left

parts.note: everyone means all

explanation.surface: Everyone supported a ship's mission to stamp out piracy on the oceans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' turns the fodder into CAPIRY, which the reversed piece cuts after its fourth letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A capillary is a tiny blood vessel; 'Vessel' with piracy and the sea suggests a ship.

clue.text: Lines eg spider's woven to trap insects at the centre

indicators.note: the shuffled letters catch the middle letter inside them
the letters are woven together into a new pattern, like a web
the middle letter of insects is taken

explanation.surface: A spider spins its web to catch insects in the middle.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's in spider's is a short 'is'. 'woven' rearranges EG SPIDER; 'to trap' puts E, the centre of INSECTS, inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Pedigrees are lines of descent, the recorded ancestry of animals or families.

clue.text: A ring arrested in hustling and vice prevention

indicators.note: the ring letter is held, like a prisoner, inside the other letters
hustling means pushing roughly about, so the letters are jostled into a new order

parts.note: a ring is round, the shape of the letter O

explanation.surface: A criminal ring is arrested for hustling and vice, to prevent more crime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hustling' rearranges AND VICE into VIDANCE; O goes inside after V.
explanation.definitionFit: Avoidance of something means keeping it from happening, so it is a synonym of prevention.

clue.text: Beckoned single lad nervously

indicators.note: acting nervously means fidgeting, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A young unattached man waves someone over, a little anxiously.
explanation.definitionFit: To beckon is to make a gesture or sign asking someone to come, which is a way of signalling.

clue.text: Defeated politician (bridge player) in poker game

indicators.note: the politician and player go inside the card game

parts.note: stud is a form of poker
MP is a Member of Parliament
in bridge the four players are North, South, East and West, so E is East

explanation.surface: A politician and a bridge player sit down at a poker table and lose.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a batter is stumped when the wicketkeeper breaks the wicket; here it means baffled.
explanation.definitionFit: Being stumped means being baffled or beaten by a problem, so defeated fits.

clue.text: Slaver keeping Australian native in confines of domicil

indicators.note: the outer letters keep the animal between them
the first and last letters of domicil are used, like the walls of a home

parts.note: a roo, short for kangaroo, is native to Australia

explanation.surface: A slave-trader holds an Aboriginal Australian captive at home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slaver' looks like a slave trader, but it is the verb to dribble. The clue's 'domicil' is cut short so its outer letters are D and L.
explanation.definitionFit: To slaver is to let saliva run from the mouth, which is to dribble.

clue.text: I'm surprised about learner driver being magnificent

indicators.note: the exclamation goes round the learner letter

parts.note: Lordy is an exclamation of surprise
L is the learner plate on a British car

explanation.surface: Someone is amazed that a learner driver looks so splendid.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a learner driver displays an L plate.
explanation.definitionFit: Lordly means grand and noble in manner, like a lord, so splendid or magnificent.

clue.text: Honest post

definitions.meaning: an honest, upstanding person is morally straight
a vertical post or beam, standing straight up, is one in building

explanation.surface: A short pairing that suggests a truthful message or job posting.
explanation.definitionFit: One word means both morally upstanding and a vertical support such as a post.

clue.text: Mature and frail, peeing regularly

indicators.note: every other letter of these words is taken, starting with the second

explanation.surface: Someone elderly and frail needs the toilet often.
explanation.definitionFit: To mature means to grow fully developed, as fruit does when it ripens.

clue.text: March in exercise that's upwards trudge

indicators.note: in a down clue, the whole piece reads from bottom to top
the month goes inside the exercise abbreviation

parts.note: PT is physical training, school exercise

explanation.surface: Marching uphill during training is a hard slog.
explanation.walkthrough: The inner build is PMART, which 'that's upwards' turns round in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: To tramp is to walk heavily and wearily, a synonym of trudge.

clue.text: Attempt articles in two languages and fail

parts.note: to have a go is to make an attempt
un is a French indefinite article and der a German definite article

explanation.surface: Someone tries translating articles into two languages and makes a hash of it.
explanation.definitionFit: A business that goes under collapses or fails.

clue.text: River leaving the capital is brown

indicators.note: the capital letter, the first one, leaves the word

parts.note: the Humber is an estuary river in north-east England

explanation.surface: A river flows out of the capital city and runs brown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the capital' suggests a city such as London, but it means the word's first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Umber is a natural earth pigment of a dark brown shade.

clue.text: Stationery's worthless stuff, returned note with report of damage

indicators.note: the next piece is placed alongside

parts.note: pap is trivial, worthless reading matter

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the letters read in reverse

parts.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: wear is damage from use, as in wear and tear

explanation.surface: An office supplier's goods are rubbish, sent back with a note complaining of damage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns RE into ER; 'report of' makes WEAR sound like WARE.
explanation.definitionFit: Paperware means articles made of paper, such as the writing materials sold as stationery.

clue.text: Prohibit aluminium for flat

parts.note: to prohibit is to ban
Al is the chemical symbol for aluminium

explanation.surface: A ban on aluminium in apartments, or for flat sheets of metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Flat in the sense of dull and lifeless is a synonym of trite or uninspired.

clue.text: Rogue insider has to admit pinching expired items from bakery

indicators.note: the shuffled letters pinch the next word, holding it between them
rogue means behaving wildly, so the letters break out of order

parts.note: something expired is past, over and done

explanation.surface: A dishonest insider has to own up to stealing out-of-date stock from a bakery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rogue' makes DANISHRIES from the fodder; 'to admit' just links the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Danish pastries are sweet flaky pastries sold by bakers.
